text:
Ana (Sales): Hey team — Sable is asking for a 'staggered burst' option on their Dedicated contract. They want the ability to shift unused burst between weeks and across regions within a month, and they want clarity on how that affects our buffer policy and SLA. Anyone seen this before?
Maya R (Infra): We’ve had one customer ask something similar but not exactly cross-region. Key questions: what base commit are they signing for, and what HW (A100/H100)?
Ana (Sales): They’re looking at 250 GPU-hours/month committed (mostly A100), and they want to allow bursts up to ~1200 GPU-hours in a month if needed, but spreadable (i.e., if they don’t use week1 burst they want to move it to week4).
David K (Capacity): That’s a big spread. From a capacity planning POV we treat commits as reserved footprint for scheduling; bursts are best-effort. Cross-region shifting adds complexity because we reserve per-region pools.
Priya S (CS): Sable is a finance customer, cares about predictability. They want a simple amortized price: fixed charge for commit + credits for burst that can roll over within month.
Luis (CloudOps): Rolling burst across regions means we either over-provision global headroom or use soft caps + automated failover. Both have different cost profiles.
Maya R (Infra): Short answer: we can do a month-level burst pool (single bucket) that is region-aware, but we need policy: 1) per-request routing preference, 2) fallback order, 3) hard cap per-region to avoid noisy-neighboring other customers.
David K (Capacity): Quick calc I did:
```
Committed: 250 GPU-hrs/mo
Requested max-month: 1,200 GPU-hrs/mo
Burstable = 950 GPU-hrs (380% of commit)
If average sustained daily peak is 20 GPUs for 6 hours x 5 days = 600 GPU-hrs (example)
We'd need an expected extra headroom ~600 GPU-hrs across the month to satisfy that tail.
```
Ana (Sales): They asked if we can guarantee 95% availability for burst capacity during business hours (Mon-Fri 08:00-18:00 PST).
Luis (CloudOps): Guarantees on burst are tricky — we can SLA reserved commit. For burst we can offer an "SLA-backed burst allocation" with a smaller committed pool in our orchestration and pay a premium; essentially convert some burst into pseudo-reserved windows. That means higher cost.
Priya S (CS): Suggested commercial option: Tier A: standard commit + non-guaranteed burst (cheaper), Tier B: commit + guaranteed burst windows (higher price), Tier C: fully reserved for peak (highest). Sable prefers Tier B if cost delta < 25%.
Maya R (Infra): Operationally we need to define enforcement rules. My proposal:
- Rolling monthly burst bucket (can be used region-to-region)
- Per-region soft cap = 50% of that bucket to protect local clusters
- If soft cap exceeded, requests try other regions per routing policy for customer
- If failover fails, return 429 with clear billing note

David K (Capacity): Also add a smoothing policy: if the customer spikes >X for >Y hours, throttle to protect 99th percentile of others. We need parameterized knobs for billing and safety.
Ana (Sales): Can we put numbers we can present tomorrow? They want a ballpark price difference between Tier A and Tier B.
Luis (CloudOps): Rough cost differential: converting 300 GPU-hrs of burst into guaranteed window (~reserve in control plane) costs roughly 30-40% of the committed per-hour unit (because of allocation inefficiency). So Tier B premium estimate: +20-35% on monthly bill, depending on region (e.g., EMEA spots higher).
Maya R (Infra): For the SLA text we should say: "Guaranteed burst availability subject to regional hard caps and scheduled maintenance; routing may shift to alternate regions which may increase latency." Keep legal happy.
Priya S (CS): Also flag compliance: since they’re finance, they want logs of burst allocations, timestamps, and audit trail. Ops-bot can dump allocation events.
ops-bot: Allocation logs for customer_sable will be available at https://console.redwood/internal/allocs/sable (read-only) :lock: 
David K (Capacity): One more thing: if they want carryover across months we should disallow — carryover to next billing cycle creates long-term capacity churn. Keep roll-over only within billing month.
Ana (Sales): Great. Action items?
Maya R (Infra): I’ll draft the operational policy and soft/hard cap numbers by EOD.
David K (Capacity): I’ll run a Monte Carlo over their usage trace to recommend a conservative burst bucket size and failure probability. Need Sable usage sample.
Priya S (CS): I’ll ask Sable for 6 months of anonymized hourly usage and confirm regions (US-WEST, EU-CENTRAL).
Luis (CloudOps): I’ll price the premium per-region and give a two-line blurb on latency impact.
Ana (Sales): Thanks all — I’ll sync with Sable after we have numbers. :thumbsup:
Maya R (Infra): One quick note — if they insist on H100 for bursts we need to re-evaluate costs; H100 capacity is narrower. Mentioned in case Sable asks for model-specific guarantees.
Ana (Sales): noted.
Luis (CloudOps): ops-bot will simulate a tentative allocation window for the proposed month later tonight and post results here.
ops-bot: Simulation started: scenario_id=sim-20260318-01. ETA 35m.
Ana (Sales): awesome, will keep thread open.
